title: Integrate unsat-core fallback

scope.assurance_scope: PCSM Python v1 unsat-core fallback capability assessment for the exact current admitted source forest
scope.implementation_delta: The exact current ipfs_datasets source forest already supplies the reusable ValidatedCraigInterpolation@1 authority. Its versioned fallback computes an independently core-validated Z3 UNSAT result for A and B when the qualified cvc5 interpolation path is unavailable or unqualified, binds named partitions and their canonical term CIDs to the fallback result receipt, and returns status=fallback with no interpolant. The declared-output boundary permits only this receipt, so no duplicate fallback, solver adapter, source mutation, or competing PCSM authority was created.
scope.non_promotion_reason: The existing implementation and dedicated positive/negative tests are present and pass in the provider environment, but the authoritative sealed environment has neither cvc5 nor z3 Python APIs, so the fallback itself is typed unavailable there. The sealed required pytest command also cannot collect because its explicitly configured anyio plugin is absent. No canonical PCSM current-source-map CID binds PCSM source nodes/spans to a fallback request. This receipt therefore records the current-head reusable capability without claiming a sealed fallback result or promotion.

evidence_legend.measured: Observed directly from the named current source forest or the authoritative sealed validation environment.
evidence_legend.estimated: A calculated approximation; it cannot establish source identity, solver behavior, CID binding, or validation success.
evidence_legend.simulated: A controlled provider-environment execution; it cannot replace sealed validation or authorize promotion.
evidence_legend.unavailable: A required identity, capability, or result absent from the authoritative environment; it is neither zero nor passing.

pcsm_source_map.reason: No current-tree aggregate PCSM source-map CID or canonical CodeIR/source identity resolving exact PCSM file/node/span identities is present in the named implementation/test roots. ValidatedCraigInterpolation@1 binds structural SMT partitions with canonical term CIDs and names its fallback assertions, but it cannot manufacture the absent PCSM source identity; Git trees, blobs, term CIDs, and local test node IDs are not substitutes.

components.role: Capability-negotiated QF_LIA interpolation authority. It uses cvc5 only as the declared producer and Z3 only as an independent validator or typed UNSAT-core fallback; solver availability is not interpolation qualification.

For an unavailable or unqualified interpolation producer, it submits named partition-a and partition-b assertions to the existing IncrementalSmtSession@1 path. It emits a fallback receipt only after result.status is UNSAT and result.core_validated is true; satisfiable, unknown, rejected, absent-validator, and provider errors remain typed non-success.

Existing reusable session selected by the fallback. It binds named assertions, source_ref values, obligation IDs, deterministic session fingerprints, canonical result identities, and independently rechecked sorted UNSAT cores; it does not treat a core as a theorem proof.
Checked public facade for the selected interpolation/fallback authority; no parallel PCSM facade was introduced.

determinism_and_binding.profile: InterpolationBounds fixes timeout, memory, symbol, term-node, theory, and schema values. The request root canonically binds partition-A CID, partition-B CID, provider version, and theory. Fallback assertions use stable names partition-a and partition-b, term-CID source_ref values, and obligation_id=core-fallback. ValidatedInterpolantReceipt sorts vocabulary, limitations, and fallback core entries, rejects a fallback containing an interpolant, requires fallback_validated/fallback_kind/fallback_receipt for status=fallback, and derives receipt_cid with canonical_identity under validated-craig-interpolant/v1.
determinism_and_binding.authority_boundary: The core is diagnostic fallback authority only: fallback limitations explicitly include fallback_is_not_an_interpolant. A validated interpolant requires separate A=>I, I-and-B UNSAT, vocabulary, identity, and bounds checks. Opening/using the fallback does not install a solver, manufacture a PCSM source link, supply a kernel proof, or authorize mutation or promotion.
determinism_and_binding.current_pcsm_execution_binding: unavailable because a canonical PCSM source-map/CID and usable sealed cvc5/z3 capabilities are both absent.

source_inventory.role: Versioned qualified interpolation authority, independently validated unsat-core fallback implementation, receipt schema/status invariants, canonical partition/interpolant identities, and sealed-capability probe.
Existing session/result/replay authority used to bind and independently validate the fallback UNSAT core.
Public checked facade that exposes the selected interpolation/fallback authority.
Dedicated positive and negative interpolation/fallback contract coverage.
Dedicated positive and negative deterministic named-session and independently rechecked UNSAT-core coverage used by the fallback.

positive_coverage: A qualified cvc5 QF_LIA interpolant is independently checked with fresh Z3 sessions, has canonical partition/interpolant/receipt CIDs, and retains only shared vocabulary.

An unavailable mathsat producer and an unqualified z3 producer both produce status=fallback only when the named A-and-B core is independently validated; fallback_core is bounded to the named partition assertions and fallback_receipt is content addressed.

Repeated admission produces a stable receipt identity, and IncrementalSmtSession coverage verifies sorted independently rechecked cores, source/obligation binding, scoped state, deterministic replay identities, and public interface checks.
negative_coverage: A fallback receipt cannot contain an interpolant and cannot omit validated fallback authority; a core is never called an interpolant.

Unknown or absent independent validators, absent/unqualified producers, jointly satisfiable partitions, invalid vocabulary, invalid implication, invalid I-and-B inconsistency, malformed requests, oversized terms, unsupported theory, and closed/cancelled/stale session states remain typed rejection, unavailable, unsupported, invalid, or unknown outcomes.
Importing the interpolation module leaves optional solver modules cold; fallback use neither installs a provider nor permits arbitrary proof output as authority.
positive_and_negative_test_sources.coverage_limit: The dedicated tests validate reusable interpolation/fallback and incremental-session behavior. They do not create a PCSM source-map-bound obligation, prove a theorem in a kernel, or turn a solver observation into mutation authority.

limitations: This exact-output dispatch is receipt-only. It selects and validates an existing current-head authority but does not modify datasets implementation/tests or create a competing fallback subsystem.
A fallback core is not an interpolant, theorem certificate, kernel proof, or source mutation authority. It is emitted only after the existing session reports UNSAT and core_validated=true.

The sole qualified interpolation producer is cvc5/QF_LIA and the independent fallback/validation adapter is Z3. Both Python APIs are absent in the authoritative sealed environment; provider-environment solvers do not satisfy that gate.
Canonical structural SMT term CIDs bind fallback partitions, but they do not establish PCSM current-forest file/node/span identity until a separate canonical PCSM source-map/CID authority exists.
The required PCSM suite cannot collect in the sealed environment and the provider invocation's terminal summary was not retained; neither result is a sealed package-validation pass.
No model output is accepted as evidence or mutation authority, and no M2/M3 mutation, generated-source mutation, automatic source materialization, or promotion is authorized.
The receipt has no immutable self-CID because minting a self-describing CID would change its bytes.
